newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain soft wheat, barley helped by recent rain.
newsitem.headline: Spain soft wheat, barley helped by recent rain.

text.p: Spain's soft wheat and barley harvest this year is likely to be around a third less than 1996's exceptional crop in the main production area following three days of rainfall after months of dry weather.

"A lot of people have been talking about crop losses this year, but after the recent rain that's not relevant. The harvest isn't going to match last year because last year was exceptional. But at this point it should still be a good harvest," said Eduardo Garcia, a technical expert at a farmers association in the Castille-Leon autonomous region.
The region produced around 2.1 million tonnes of soft wheat and 4.6 million tonnes of barley in 1996, according to latest Agriculture Ministry estimates, and is the key area for these crops in Spain.
Total barley output last year was 10.6 million tonnes while soft wheat was around 4.5 million in the country as a whole.
Garcia estimated that Castille-Leon's barley and soft wheat production will be around a third less than last year, although more wet weather was necessary to guarantee this harvest level.

"The rain arrived at a critical point, and it saved the situation, which was becoming grave. Of course we're still going to need more rain from this point, but for the moment it looks good," Garcia told Reuters.
Soft wheat and barley harvesting starts around June in the region and runs through until August.
Traders said prices had shown no signs of weakening yet, with all grains static at last week's levels.
"For prices to go down we need the farmers to come out and sell. Theoretically, they're holding back supplies, but nobody really knows how much there is," said one in Barcelona.
"But one day or another they will have to sell, and that's when we'll see prices come off," he said.
